issue.title: ledger-tools gcal-events and freshness-namespace tests read the real date and fail from 2026-10-31
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-eq.7 (note #3, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP) and routed by the bob-cli-eq land agent.
Not caused by bob-cli-eq: the epic never touched bob-ledger-tools.

Two bob-plugins Node tests fail deterministically from 2026-10-31 onward because each
depends partly on the real wall-clock date:

- `scripts/test-ledger-tools-gcal-events.cjs` > "create listener runs once for today's
  note after layout readiness" (line ~152). The test pins `now = new Date(2026, 9, 30, 9)`
  and creates `todayDailyPath(now)`, but the plugin's create listener compares against the
  real current day, so `syncs` is 0, not 1 (line ~176).
- `scripts/test-ledger-tools-freshness-namespace.cjs` > "the reload event fires only when
  the due key set changes" (line ~294). The task is stamped `[fresh:: 2026-10-01]`. Moving
  to a 30-day interval was meant to clear the ROTTEN entry. But
  `refreshFreshnessForChangedFile` evaluates against the real clock, where the task is due
  again on 2026-10-31. The due set never changes, so no reload event fires
  (`[] !== ['obsidian-tasks-plugin:reload-open-search-results']`, line ~317).

Proof that the date causes both: with `Date` pinned by a `--require` preload, both files
pass 17/17 at 2026-10-30T12:00 and fail exactly these 2 at 2026-10-31T12:00. Both also
fail on older commits run today (5ba4683, 1295e52, c391a0d, 4e31220, and for
freshness-namespace 1295e52^).

Fix: inject or pin the plugin clock in both tests, for example the plugin's `now()` seam
or the date passed to the code under test, so neither reads the real date. Do not change
the production behavior.

This is distinct from bob-cli-eh. That task covers the single-slot onLayoutReady fake in
test-ledger-tools-note-ready.cjs and test-ledger-tools-relation-index.cjs.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Fails on every run dated 2026-10-31 and passes on every run with Date pinned to 2026-10-30, on the same tree (8ef763a) and on older commits; the failing assertions compare against the real current day.
